svg.aria-label: Allele frequency trajectories for dominant additive and recessive beneficial alleles, and the reciprocal-frequency law for selection against a recessive
svg.text: Haldane’s sieve: same benefit (s = 0.01), utterly different fates
generations →
allele frequency
dominant (h = 1)
additive (h = ½)
recessive (h = 0)
The recessive allele lingers near zero for hundreds of generations,
because Δq ≈ s q²p and q² is negligible when q is small.
In a real finite population, drift kills it long before it gets going.
Fixation probability ≈ 2s for a dominant, ≈ 1/(2N) — the neutral
value — for a recessive of identical benefit.
So new alleles that sweep should be dominant or additive.
(The sieve applies to NEW mutations, not to standing variation —
and not in selfers, where homozygotes appear immediately.)
Complete selection against a recessive: 1/q rises by exactly 1 per generation
generations →
1/qᵗ = 1/q₀ + t

the same data, as a frequency
each tenfold reduction takes
ten times as long as the last
Selection sees the allele only in homozygotes,
and at q = 0.02 that is 2% of the copies.
